headline: Alignment-free ANI-based annotation of tandem repeat arrays and satellite DNA
label: Tandem Repeat Genome Annotation
summary: Long-read sequencing now enables catalog-scale annotation of repeat arrays, while benchmarks expose method-dependent annotation variation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is annotation of repeat-rich and variable genomic regions, where annotation choices materially shape downstream conclusions. AniAnns, a preprint, annotates tandem repeat arrays and satellite DNA without alignment by estimating average nucleotide identity between repeat units. A pangenome analysis reports that gene presence-absence variation often reflects annotation method differences rather than sequence differences. A benchmark of five nanopore direct RNA annotation tools on barley infected with net blotch reports variable isoform annotation across tools. PolyAseqTrap identifies and quantifies polyadenylation sites from diverse 3' sequencing data, and piRAT annotates primary piRNAs from clusters and secondary piRNAs via ping-pong cycles. What is new is a shift toward reproducible, method-aware characterization of repetitive and variable sequence, in which tool-dependent calls are themselves evaluated. These items do not address transposon-mediated regulation.
